newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northwest next-day power up, Southwest lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northwest next-day power up, Southwest lower.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the northwestern U.S. for Wednesday delivery rose against Monday's level, while those in the Southwest fell.

Despite seasonal weather in the region, a frenzy to meet demand over the Thanksgiving holiday weekend and firm daily offers from Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) bolstered values in the Northwest,
BPA offered peak-load power for Friday and Saturday at $32.00 a megawatt hour in the Northwest and $32.75 at the California-Oregon Border (COB), flat from Monday's offers.
Unconfirmed reports of a 300 megawatt (MW) generating unit tripping off line Monday also helped lift prices at key delivery points in the Northwest.
Firm, peak COB electricity for Wednesday was quoted at $31.75-$32.25, firmer than Monday's $30.00-$32.00 for Tuesday delivery

Firm, off-peak COB power for Wednesday was notationally pegged at $17.00-$18.00, compared with $16.50-$17.50 Monday December COB deliveries were assessed at $28.25-$29.25, up from $27.50-$28.50 Monday. January COB rose to $25.25-$25.50, sharply higher than Monday's $23.50-$24.25.
First-quarter 1997 COB was valued at $21.25-$21.40 up from $20.00-$20.25 Monday.
Next-day firm, peak power at Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) was discussed at $30.75-$31.25, up from Monday's $29.00-$31.00.
Next-day firm, off-peak Mid-C values were notationally talked at $18.50-$19.50, compared with $18.00-$19.00 Monday.
December Mid-C was quoted at $27.00-$28.00, up from Monday's quote of $25.50-$26.00. January 1997 Mid-C was pegged at $23.50-$24.50, up from $23.45-$24.00 Monday.
Down in the Southwest, next-day power deliveries opened strongly amid higher natgas prices at the San Juan/Blanco Hub.
December San Juan gas ended today at $3.61-$3.65 per million British thermal units, up from $3.45 Monday.
A late sell-off pushed next-day prices at Palo Verde (PV) and Four Corners sharply lower, marketers and.
Wednesday firm, peak PV power ended at $20.00-$21.00 after opening at $28.00-$29.00. The late Tuesday quote was much lower than Monday's $28.50-$30.00.
Wednesday firm, off-peak PV electricity was quoted at $13.00-$14.00, down from 1$15.00-$17.00 Monday.
December PV power was assessed at $27.00-$28.00, a tighter range than Monday's $26.75-$28.00. January PV was valued at $24.00-$25.00, higher than Monday's $22.90-$23.50.
First-quarter 1997 PV deliveries were discussed at $21.50-$21.90.
Four Corners firm, peak power for Wednesday ended at $21.00-$23.00, off sharply in tandem with PV prices from Monday's $29.00-$31.00 Tuesday.
Four Corners firm, off-peak power for Wednesday was notationally assessed at $14.00-$17.00, compared with Monday's $16.00-$18.00.

The 1,087 MW Diablo Canyon nuclear 1 nuclear unit in central California was scheduled to resume operation by Friday after tripping off line November 22 when a fire hit an auxiliary power grounding transformer.
--R Leong, New York Power Desk +1 212 859 1622
